calls.head: Sheltered vs. exposed
calls.body: The Kraken keep dangerous shots away, but the Ducks give up a lot of them. Seattle is the league’s best for preventing dangerous shots, and Anaheim is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances should come at the Ducks’ net.

surprises.head: Anaheim found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Seattle is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Not tonight: Anaheim’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (about 5.8% against Seattle) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Kakko wins it with two and a half minutes left
paras: The Kraken went more than 17 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the second to early in the third, while the Ducks put eight on net. The third period brought five goals. Ben Meyers struck first for the Kraken early in the period, but Cutter Gauthier made it 1-1 for Anaheim a little over a minute later. Vince Dunn put the Kraken back ahead 2-1 midway through the period. Sam Colangelo tied it 2-2 for Anaheim with less than eight minutes left, with Stian Solberg picking up his first NHL point on the goal. Kaapo Kakko put the Kraken ahead for good with two and a half minutes left.

The Ducks had a little more of the play and hit a post and the crossbar, but the Kraken had the finish. Joey Daccord made 24 saves for the Kraken, and Lukáš Dostál stopped 18 of 21 at the other end. The Kraken moved to 11-9-1 and took fourth place in the Pacific from the Ducks, who fell to 11-13-1.
